name: Dining chairs and stools
tagline: A seat, four legs, a back. You will build the same chair two or four times, so the first one is practice.
covers: Dining chairs sold in pairs or sets of four
peopleNote: One person. Per chair, not for the set.

tools.why: Seat plates and some back brackets.
To work on, so you do not scuff the seat fabric or the leg finish.

before: Open only one chair's hardware bag at a time. Mixing four sets of look-alike bolts is a mess you do not need.
Build the first chair slowly and the rest will take five minutes each.
Work on a towel. Chair legs are usually the most visible finish in the box.
safety: A chair bolt that is only finger-tight will fail with someone sitting on it. Final tightening is not optional.
Do not stand on a chair you just built until you have tightened everything and sat on it first.

steps.title: Turn the seat upside down on a towel
steps.say: Put the seat upside down on a folded towel. Everything bolts to the underside, and this way gravity helps instead of fighting you.
do: Seat upside down, padded surface
Threaded inserts or bracket holes facing up
All four legs within reach

steps.title: Sort front legs from back legs
steps.say: On most chairs the back legs are longer, because they continue upward to become the back. Match them to the manual before bolting anything.
do: Longer pair, or the pair with extra holes, goes at the back
Check for L and R markings on the back legs
Lay them out in position first
steps.watch: Front legs in the back sockets is the single most common chair mistake, and it is invisible until the chair is finished and leans.

steps.title: Start every bolt before tightening any
steps.say: Thread all the leg bolts in with their washers, just a few turns each. Loose everywhere. Nothing tight yet.
do: Washer between bolt and wood or metal, always
Thread by hand first to feel the threads catch
All bolts started before any are tightened
steps.watch: If a bolt will not start by hand, back it out. Forcing it with the Allen key strips the insert and that leg is then permanently loose.

steps.title: Fit the back or backrest
steps.say: The back either bolts onto the rear legs or drops into brackets. Get all its bolts started loosely too, then check it is centered and square.
do: Line the back up with both rear legs
All bolts started loosely
Sight along it to check it is not twisted
steps.tip: Look at the chair from the front. A back that leans to one side now will lean forever once tightened.

steps.title: Stand it up, then tighten diagonally
steps.say: Set the chair upright on a flat floor, press down on the seat to settle everything, then tighten in a diagonal pattern. Two laps.
do: Chair on a flat floor, press the seat down firmly
Front-left, back-right, front-right, back-left
Second full lap
steps.tip: Pressing the seat down while you tighten is what makes the difference between a chair that stays tight for years and one that is wobbly in a month.

steps.title: Kill the rock with the glides
steps.say: Press each corner of the seat. If it rocks, the plastic glides or felt pads let you fix it — add a second pad on the short leg.
do: Press each corner to find the short leg
Tap plastic glides fully in
Double up a felt pad under the short leg if needed
steps.tip: Felt pads on every leg are worth doing anyway. They protect the floor and they stop the dragging noise that drives everyone mad.

steps.title: Sit in it and bounce
steps.say: Sit down and shift your weight around. Any creak or movement means one more pass with the Allen key.
do: Sit, lean back, shift side to side
Listen for creaks
Re-tighten anything that moved
steps.watch: Do this before anyone else sits in it. A chair is one of the few pieces of furniture that fails with someone on it.

steps.title: Build the rest from memory
steps.say: Now you know the chair. The second one takes five minutes. Open one hardware bag at a time and repeat exactly the same order.
do: One hardware bag per chair
Same order every time
Same tightening pattern
steps.tip: Put the finished chairs in the next room as you go. It keeps your workspace clear and stops you mixing up parts.

steps.title: Re-tighten everything in two weeks
steps.say: Set a reminder. Wood and upholstery compress slightly in the first weeks of use. One tightening pass then and the chairs will stay solid for years.
do: Phone reminder for two weeks out
One lap with the Allen key on every chair
Keep the Allen key taped under one seat
steps.tip: Taping the Allen key under a seat is the single best piece of furniture advice there is. You will always know where it is.

fixes.q: The chair wobbles and will not stop
fixes.a: Loosen everything, stand the chair on a flat floor, press hard on the seat, and retighten in a diagonal pattern. Nine times out of ten it was tightened while upside down and the joints settled crooked.

fixes.q: One leg is shorter than the others
fixes.a: Usually it is not — the chair is just assembled slightly out of square. Try the retightening trick first. If it genuinely is short, double up a felt pad.

fixes.q: A bolt spins and will not tighten
fixes.a: The threaded insert in the wood has pulled loose. Pull it out, add a drop of two-part epoxy around it, push it back and let it cure overnight before bolting.

fixes.q: The back leans to one side
fixes.a: Loosen the back bolts, hold it straight while looking from the front, and retighten evenly, alternating sides.

fixes.q: The chair creaks when I sit
fixes.a: A joint is slightly loose. Creaking is wood or metal moving against wood. Find it by sitting and shifting while a helper listens, then tighten that bolt.
